definition: Accumulate means to build up little by little — to gather and grow, addition by addition, over time.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word accumulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know accumulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Snow accumulated on the fire escape all afternoon, a dry inch an hour, until the railing wore a thick white sleeve.
Collect is lighter than accumulate: you collect a few shells in one afternoon and the gathering ends, while accumulating is the slow pile that keeps growing for months or years.
Stockpile goes further than accumulate: what merely accumulates can pile up on its own, but a stockpile is built deliberately, crate by crate, against a future need.

to build up a great store, usually on purpose — fortunes, armies, and archives get amassed. Accumulate is quieter and more patient: it works addition by addition, and the pile can grow with nobody intending it at all.

to stash a supply away and guard it from use — hoarding is about the keeping, with a fist closed over the pile. Accumulating is about the growing; what accumulates may be spent, shoveled, or deleted tomorrow.
to use up bit by bit until little remains
to scatter or spend wastefully

Iben's team drills two hundred meters into the Greenland ice sheet and pulls up a core striped like tree rings.
Each stripe is one year of snowfall.
Snow does not melt here; it settles, packs down, and slowly turns to ice under the weight of the layers above.
Nobody plans this archive.
The sheet simply accumulates a few centimeters of new ice a year, and has done so, layer upon layer, for a hundred thousand years.
Ash from old volcanoes, pollen, even traces of Roman smelting arrive on the wind and are pressed into the record one thin season at a time.
Asked why the core matters, Iben taps the oldest stripe: small additions, given enough centuries, become the longest history book on Earth.
